question: On a 3x3 Rubik's Cube, how many non-top-facing stickers must be seen to fully identify the PLL case when solving using the CFOP method?

2.text:
In CFOP the OLL step leaves the U face monochromatic.  The whole
distinguishing information of the last layer is therefore carried by the
side of the U–layer and not by the U face itself.

The U–layer is

* 4 U–edges : U + one side face  → 1 non–U sticker per edge,
* 4 U–corners : U + two side faces → 2 non–U stickers per corner,

i.e. 

$4\times1+4\times2=12$ non–U stickers, 8 distinct U–cubies.  Up to a
U–rotation the 21 PLL classes are the permutations of those eight
U–cubies.  In practice you never have to look at the whole 12 stickers,
the permutation of the four U–edges and the permutation of the four
U–corners determine each other up to the usual cube parity.  In
particular the four edge side stickers and one side sticker per corner,
i.e. eight different side stickers of the U–layer, are enough to name
the class; seven of them are independent, the eighth being forced by
parity.  This is the 4 edge + 4 corner side information that is normally
quoted as the “side’’ information of a PLL.  Counting both side stickers
of a corner this is the 12 side stickers of the U–layer, the 8 cubies
that are normally referred to as the 8 non–U stickers of the PLL.

1.text:
In the CFOP last layer both the U corners and the U edges are already
oriented, the whole U face is one colour.  The only thing that is left
to know is where the 8 different U-layer cubies are, 4 edges $e_{i}$ and
4 corners $c_{i}$.

A U edge is identified by the single side sticker that it carries,
the colour that you see on the $F,R,B,L$ face at the top of the edge
is the colour of the edge cubie that is now in that U position.
A U corner is identified by the two side stickers it carries, one of
them is enough to know which corner cubie is now in that U position,
the other side sticker is the one you see on the adjacent side face.

Hence, in order to know the permutation of the last layer you have to
know the side colour of

* the 4 U edges – 1 non-U sticker per edge;
* the 4 U corners – 1 non-U sticker per corner,

i.e. one non-U identifying sticker for each of the eight U-layer
pieces.  That is the $4+4=8$ side stickers of the top layer that are
normally used for PLL recognition,

$$
4\;{\rm edge\;side\;stickers}+4\;{\rm corner\;side\;stickers}=12
\;{\rm side\;stickers\;on\;the\;U\;layer},
$$

and eight of them, one per piece, are enough for the identification.
Parity of the cube makes the eight stickers not quite independent:
the permutation of the four U corners has the same parity as the
permutation of the four U edges, so once seven of the eight side
stickers are known the eighth is forced.  It is for that reason that
the eight-sticker, i.e. in the strict information-theoretic sense
seven-sticker, recognition is conventionally quoted as the
$4+4$ side-sticker PLL recognition.  The twelve side stickers of the
U layer are

$4\;{\rm edges}\times1+4\;{\rm corners}\times2=12$,

the practically used set being the eight identifying stickers, four
edge and four corner, described above.  This is the usual $8$-sticker
$=$ $7$-independent-sticker PLL recognition.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: Both colleagues agree the U face is monochromatic after OLL, so all distinguishing information for PLL is carried by the side stickers of the U-layer.

U-layer sticker inventory:
* 4 U-edges: U + 1 side → 1 non-U sticker per edge, 4 total
* 4 U-corners: U + 2 sides → 2 non-U stickers per corner, 8 total
→ 12 non-U stickers are present on the U-layer, 8 distinct U-cubies.

Recognition claim:
* Edge permutation is carried by the 4 edge side stickers, one per edge.
* Corner permutation can be carried by one side sticker per corner; the second side sticker is redundant for identification up to the usual U rotation.
Conventionally quoted as 4 edge side stickers + 4 corner side stickers = 8 identifying non-U stickers.

Information-theoretic nuance noted by both:
The four U-edge and four U-corner permutations have the same parity, so the eight identifying stickers are not independent. Once seven of them are known the eighth is forced by parity. This is often described as an 8-sticker, 7-independent-sticker recognition. Total side stickers on the U-layer remain 12, i.e. 4×1+4×2.

No disagreement between colleagues on the 8-sticker conventional count / 7-independent count. Unresolved for final answer is whether the question wants the conventional 8 stickers, the information-theoretic minimum 7, or the total 12 non-U stickers physically present on the U-layer. Current understanding favours the conventional 8-sticker, 7-independent description.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The CFOP last layer after OLL has a monochromatic U face, so all distinguishing information for PLL is on the side of the U-layer.

* The U-layer contains 4 U-edges, each with 1 non-U sticker, and 4 U-corners, each with 2 non-U stickers.
  4×1 + 4×2 = 12 non-U stickers are physically present on the U-layer. That is the 12 side stickers colleagues 1 and 2 quote.

* Identification of the permutation:
  - A U-edge is uniquely identified by its single side colour; 1 non-U sticker per edge is sufficient.
  - A U-corner is defined by the unordered pair of its two side colours. In principle two side stickers per corner are needed for an unambiguous piece identity; seeing only one of the two side stickers leaves the ambiguity between the two corners that share that side colour.

Colleagues 1 and 2 both describe the conventional “identifying’’ set as one side sticker per U-cubie, i.e. 4 edge side stickers + 4 corner side stickers = 8 stickers, the usual 4+4 PLL side recognition. They note the parity coupling between the 4 U-edge permutation and the 4 U-corner permutation makes the eight stickers not independent: once seven of them are known the eighth is forced by parity. In information-theoretic terms this is quoted as a 7-independent-sticker recognition, nominally 8 stickers.

Unresolved / to keep in mind:
* Whether “one side sticker per corner is enough to know which corner cubie is now in that U position’’ is strictly correct for unique piece identification, versus needing both side stickers of a corner for unambiguous identification. The 12-sticker total is the complete side information of the U-layer.
* The question can be read as “how many non-U stickers exist on the U-layer’’ =12, vs “what is the minimal sufficient / conventionally used set’’ =8 nominally, 7 independent. Both numbers are being used in the discussion and need to be distinguished when answering.

After OLL the U face is monochromatic so the whole PLL class is carried
by the side of the U layer.

The U layer has

* 4 U edges : U + 1 side  → 1 non-U sticker per edge = 4
* 4 U corners : U + 2 sides → 2 non-U stickers per corner = 8

i.e. 4·1+4·2 = 12 non-U stickers are physically present on the U layer,
8 distinct U cubies.

With the U corners and U edges already oriented the permutation of the
last layer is the permutation of those 8 U cubies.  An U edge is
identified by the single side sticker it carries, and a U corner is
identified up to U rotation by a single side sticker of the corner,
the second side sticker of the corner being redundant for the
permutation.

Hence in practice the PLL is named by

* 4 edge side stickers, one per U edge,
* 4 corner side stickers, one per U corner,

4+4 = 8 identifying non-U stickers of the U layer, one per U-layer
piece.  The 4 edge and 4 corner permutations have the same parity, so
the eight identifying stickers are not independent.  Once seven of
them are known the eighth is forced by cube parity.  That is the
usual 8-sticker, 7-independent-sticker, 4 edge + 4 corner side
recognition that is quoted for CFOP PLL.  The 12 side stickers
4·1+4·2 of the U layer are the physical stock, the 8 of them one per
piece being the ones normally used for recognition.
